local.h: Court: family can't try US over FBI raid
local.b: An appeals court ruled an Atlanta family cannot take the government to trial over a mistaken 2017 FBI raid, but can seek to hold the agent who led the SWAT team liable.
local.title: Appeals court: Atlanta family can't take government to trial for mistaken FBI raid

local.h: Villegas González family seeks damages
local.b: The family of Silverio Villegas González, shot dead by an ICE agent during Operation Midway Blitz, filed a complaint seeking compensation from the federal government.
more: The claim under the Federal Tort Claims Act is the first step toward a lawsuit.
local.title: Family of Silverio Villegas González seeks damages over fatal ICE shooting near Chicago

local.h: Obama Center workers move to unionize
local.b: More than 250 Obama Foundation and Presidential Center workers are organizing a union with AFSCME Council 31.
more: They cite increasing workloads and benefit rollbacks.
local.title: Obama Foundation and Presidential Center workers to unionize: ‘We don't even have a seat at the table’

local.h: Chicago Marathon expects record field
local.b: Organizers expect the largest field ever for the 48th Chicago Marathon this weekend.
local.title: The Chicago Marathon is this weekend. Here’s why it’s distinctive and attracts runners

local.h: Mary Todd Lincoln's cape goes on view
local.b: The bloodstained cape Mary Todd Lincoln wore the night of Lincoln's assassination is part of a new Chicago History Museum exhibit on presidential artifacts.
local.title: Mary Todd Lincoln’s blood-soaked cape goes on view in new Chicago History Museum exhibit about presidential artifacts

local.h: Judge blocks Illinois prediction market rules
local.b: A federal judge blocked Illinois' new rules on prediction markets, a win for the app Kalshi, WBEZ reports.
more: The ruling left open the state potentially taxing transaction fees on the app.

local.h: Dodgers clinch NLDS in Atlanta
local.b: The Dodgers beat the Braves 4-1 to take the series 3-1 and move on to the NLCS, chasing a third straight World Series title.
local.title: Dodgers beat Braves 4-1 to clinch NL Division Series

local.h: US Education Dept. targets LAUSD gender policy
local.b: The U.S. Department of Education launched an enforcement action against LAUSD, alleging its gender policies keep students' gender identities from parents.
more: It cites alleged violations of federal student privacy laws including FERPA.
local.title: US Department of Education announces enforcement action against LAUSD

local.h: Suits seek air data after Lineage warehouse fire
local.b: Advocacy groups sued the EPA and the city of Los Angeles for records on possible toxic emissions from the Lineage warehouse fire in Boyle Heights, LAist reports.
more: California Communities Against Toxics says large amounts of ammonia have leaked since the fire destroyed the refrigeration system.

local.h: LA food bank strains as CalFresh cuts bite
local.b: Community Space Food Bank now sees 30 to 40 new people a day, up from two to 10, as CalFresh benefits are cut or end, LAist reports.
more: Founders Gaines and Hang Newborn are raising money to keep it open and buy its building.

local.h: Man charged in fatal Queens park stabbing
local.b: Police arrested 53-year-old Abdullah Spencerel on murder charges in a fatal stabbing in Major Mark Park in Queens.
more: A witness pointed officers to him three blocks away; police are still working to identify the victim.
local.title: Bronx man arrested for allegedly stabbing Queens man to death in a public park

local.h: Data centers stir NY governor race
local.b: Gothamist's Jimmy Vielkind writes that the New York governor race pits an old immigration playbook against new outrage over data centers.
local.title: NY gov race pits old immigration playbook against new outrage over data centers

local.h: Survey: NYC parents split on childcare needs
local.b: A New America survey of NYC families with young children found working parents need more weekend childcare, and most want to be the main caregiver in a child's first year.
more: Parents in higher-income areas near Manhattan more often prefer formal preschool for 2-year-olds than parents in the Bronx and parts of Queens.
local.title: NYC parents want affordable childcare. But they don't all want the same thing.

local.h: Arrest in deadly Bronx balcony push
local.b: Police arrested the man they say pushed a 23-year-old mother and their 8-month-old daughter from a Bronx balcony, killing the woman; he faces a murder charge.
local.title: Man who pushed his baby and her mother from a Bronx balcony arrested for murder, NYPD says

local.h: Teen, 15, shot dead in Harlem
local.b: A 15-year-old was shot and killed and a man was wounded at NYCHA's Martin Luther King Jr. Towers in Harlem; police are questioning a teen.
local.title: Harlem community of murdered 15-year-old mourns as NYPD questions teen tied to incident

local.h: Audit questions Newark school spending
local.b: An audit questioning how millions were spent in Newark's public schools led to a referral to state prosecutors, Gothamist reports.
local.title: Audit questions how millions were spent in Newark schools. GOP says it's no surprise.

local.h: Mamdani joins Oct. 7 vigil amid Union Square protests
local.b: Mayor Zohran Mamdani attended a vigil marking the Oct. 7 attack as demonstrators waving Israeli and Palestinian flags filled Union Square under heavy police presence.
local.title: Mayor Mamdani attends Oct. 7 vigil amid protests in Union Square

local.h: Queens pharmacist charged in $31M Medicaid fraud
local.b: The owner of two Jackson Heights pharmacies was arrested on charges of a $31 million Medicaid drug-buyback scheme involving HIV prescriptions, the state attorney general said.
local.title: Queens pharmacy owner charged in alleged $31M Medicaid drugs fraud

local.h: NJ finds 1,100 more flawed voter registrations
local.b: Gov. Mikie Sherrill said her administration found about 1,100 more problematic voter registrations in its probe of the state's automatic voter registration system.
more: The probe into Motor Vehicle Commission registration errors began in July.
local.title: NJ probe finds about 1,100 more problematic voter registrations

local.h: MTA to put new fare gates at 150 stations
local.b: The MTA is moving ahead with a $1.1 billion rollout of modern sliding-door fare gates after testing them at 20 subway stations over the past year.
more: Officials say the gates have proven highly effective against fare evasion.
local.title: MTA moves ahead with $1.1B plan to put modern fare gates at 150 subway stations

local.h: Suspects in detective stabbing caught in Mass.
local.b: Two suspects in last week's stabbing of an off-duty NYPD detective in the Bronx were found hiding in a basement in Lynn, Massachusetts, police said.
more: D'Angelo Caraballo, 25, and Sneider Mejia, 24, were arrested by fugitive task force detectives.
local.title: Suspects in off-duty NYPD detective's stabbing found hiding in Massachusetts basement

local.h: Delaney Hall protest figure freed from ICE
local.b: Martin Soto, the Peruvian man at the center of summer protests at Newark's Delaney Hall, was released from ICE custody after a federal judge's order.
more: The judge cited his conditions and more than 200 days in detention.
local.title: NJ immigrant at the center of Delaney Hall protests released from ICE custody

local.h: Unlicensed Bronx doctor charged with murder
local.b: Luis Rojas Cabrera, 56, now faces a depraved indifference murder charge in the death of a 27-year-old patient during an anti-aging treatment, police say.
more: He was first arrested in July, days after Elizabeth Baron died.
local.title: NYPD says unlicensed doc has been charged with murder in 27-year-old patient death

local.h: ICE arrests near 40,000 across NY and NJ
local.b: ICE has made more than 19,500 arrests in New York state and nearly 18,000 in New Jersey during Trump's second term, Gothamist reports from new government data.
more: The arrests are largely of Latin American immigrant men without criminal histories.
local.title: Nearly 40K and counting: Here’s where ICE arrested immigrants across NY and NJ

local.h: Crashes pile up on Central Park's car-free loop
local.b: Three people have died in crashes on Central Park's 6-mile loop since June as more than 100,000 people use the park each day, Gothamist reports.
more: On Monday a 71-year-old cyclist fell near 84th Street while avoiding an off-leash dog.
local.title: Central Park's car-free loop is busier than ever. Crashes keep piling up.

local.h: NYC to spend $9M on youth gender-affirming care
local.b: New York City plans to spend nearly $9 million on local groups providing gender-affirming care to minors, part of a $15 million Mamdani administration pledge.
more: It follows deals by NYU Langone and Mount Sinai with the Trump administration to stop such care for minors.
local.title: NYC moves to spend nearly $9M of gender-affirming care fund for minors

local.h: Lescure: Brexit impact "irrevocable"
local.b: Finance Minister Roland Lescure said he would welcome the UK back in the EU but warned Brexit had irrevocable consequences.
more: He said a return would mean taking "the whole thing," not special terms.
local.title: French finance minister warns of 'irrevocable' Brexit impact

local.h: TotalEnergies strike shuts some fuel stations
local.b: TotalEnergies workers are on strike Thursday, blocking shipments from refineries near Le Havre, at Donges and at La Mède, and closing some petrol stations.

local.h: Le Pen proposes tax on hiring non-EU workers
local.b: Marine Le Pen's counter-budget includes an extra €1,000 a year per worker for companies that employ non-EU nationals.
local.title: Le Pen proposes new tax on companies in France that employ foreign workers

local.h: PM Lecornu: France can't ignore student protests
local.b: In a TV address, Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said students' anger 'does not come from nowhere' and promised action on key points by the end of October.
more: He laid out areas for improvement in the education system.

local.h: French students plan new protest day Thursday
local.b: High school student unions say protests will continue Thursday, Oct. 8, as 'act four' of their movement, with classes suspended at many lycées for the rest of the week.
more: The government wants students and staff to use the days for 'internal democracy', an idea many have rejected.

local.h: Drought leaves 94,000 in France without tap water
local.b: France's environment ministry says 94,000 people are on emergency drinking water supplies due to severe drought, up from 64,000 in early September.
more: Another 6.4 million residents are on water systems placed on alert.

local.h: France suspends stun grenades at school protests
local.b: France suspended police use of stun grenades at high school protests after a teenager lost his hand to one.
more: Many high schools stay closed for the rest of the week.
Student leaders plan an 'act four' of protests on Thursday.

goodnews.h: Viral vegetarian wolf becomes a toy
goodnews.b: Intermarché will sell 700,000 plush versions of the vegetarian wolf from its viral Christmas advert at the end of November.
goodnews.title: French viral vegetarian wolf is finally appearing in toy form

local.h: Internment survivors begin march to ICE center
local.b: Japanese American survivors of WWII incarceration began a four-day pilgrimage from Seattle to the Northwest ICE Processing Center in Tacoma to protest mass deportations.
more: About 20 people, including Tule Lake camp survivor Satsuki Ina, started in the International District.
